headline: Sony to stop making disc-based PlayStation games by 2028
summary: Sony shifts to digital-only games, citing consumer preference.
details: Sony has announced it will discontinue physical game disc production for PlayStation games starting January 2028. This decision follows 'shifting trends in consumer preference' towards digital sales.
Physical game distribution accounted for only 3% of PlayStation's revenue last year. The PS5 Pro, launched in 2024, didn't include a disc drive, hinting at Sony's future plans.
The change won't affect games released or planned before January 2028. However, it may impact the second-hand game market and retailers.
Sony is also closing the PlayStation Store on PS3 and PS Vita, with store closures happening as early as August 2026 in some markets and July 2027 in the US.
caption:
Is this the end of game discs? Sony to go all-digital by 2028.

Sony has announced it will discontinue physical game disc production for PlayStation games starting January 2028. This decision follows 'shifting trends in consumer preference' towards digital sales.

Physical game distribution accounted for only 3% of PlayStation's revenue last year. The PS5 Pro, launched in 2024, didn't include a disc drive, hinting at Sony's future plans.

The change won't affect games released or planned before January 2028. However, it may impact the second-hand game market and retailers.

Sony is also closing the PlayStation Store on PS3 and PS Vita, with store closures happening as early as August 2026 in some markets and July 2027 in the US.
